r2_body: † By mercie and truth iniquitie is redemed : and in the feare ofour Lord euil is auoided. † When the wayes of man shal pleaſe our Lord, he wil connert alſo his enemies to peace. † Better isa litle with iuſtice, then much fruite with iniquitie. † The hatt of man diſpoſerh his way : bur it perteyneth to our Lord to direct his progreſſe. God aſſiſ Diuination is in the lippes of the king, his mouth shal not erre in iudgement. iheirſubiectes. † Weight and balance are iudgements of our Lord: and his Iuſt balancedo worke al the ſtones of the bagge. † They are abominable to the king that doe impiouſly : becauſe the throne is eſtablished by iuſtice. Righicouſnes. † The wil of kinges are iuſt lippes : he that ſpeaketh right thinges shal be beloued. † The kings indignation, meſſengers of death : and the wiſe man wil pacifie it. † In the cherfulnes of the kings countenance is life : and his clemencie is as the later showre. † Poſleſſe wiſdom, becauſe it is better then gold : and gette prudence, becauſe it is more precious then ſiluer. † The path of the iuſt auoideth euils: the keper of his ſoule kepeth his way. † Pride goeth before deſtruction, and before ruine the ſpirit8 shal de exalted. † Ir is beuter to be humbled with the meeke, then to diuide ſpoyles with the proude. Hope in God. † The lerned in word shal finde good thinges : and he that2o hopeth in our Lord, is bleſſed. † He thar is wiſe in hart, shal be called prudent : and he that is ſweere in ſpeach shal finde greater thinges. † A fountaine of life the ſerning of him that poſſeſſeth it: the doctrine of fooles foolishnes. † The hart of the wiſe shal inſtruct his mouth : and shal adde grace to his lippes † wel ſer wordes are a honie combe: ſwetnes of the ſoule the2 health of the bones. † There is a way that ſecmeth toa manright : and the later endes therof lead to death.
